35bf489476a86d10e9db778be16b5e0c018b5dc8.summary: IBM Security X-Force Red analysed a remote code execution flaw in Cobalt Strike 4.7.1, a command-and-control framework used in red team operations. HelpSystems issued an out-of-band patch on September 20, 2022, marked as cross-site scripting under CVE-2022-39197. X-Force found the patch insufficient, requested CVE-2022-42948 and gave the technical details to HelpSystems. The write-up covers patch analysis, root cause review and vulnerability weaponization, using Java Swing HTML handling and the Apache Batik library. It says the flaw could also be triggered through data from a real beacon.

35133d4a5776cdd31b605dbf66355e9e7b352016.summary: Technique reference page for MITRE ATT&CK T1562.002, Impair Defenses: Disable Windows Event Logging, published as an open-source catalog of detection test cases. It describes how adversaries disable Windows event logging and change audit policy to leave less evidence of compromise. It lists ten test cases covering IIS HTTP logging, audit policy, wevtutil, Phant0m and EventLog channel permissions. It names one threat group and one ransomware family that use these methods. It reports no specific incident.

35f1522128ae21490cc812f5929b961fe0cbdf5c.summary: Trustwave describes three recent investigations: two hospitality clients and one restaurant chain. It says the attacks appear to be a new Carbanak / Anunak methodology. They began with a phone-based social engineering call and a malicious Word document. The payload gathered system data and screenshots and used reconnaissance tools such as Nmap. A second-stage backdoor, bf.exe, had banking, remote desktop, password-theft and point-of-sale memory-scraping functions. At the time, existing antivirus did not detect the malware and investigations were ongoing. The report also cites CVE-2013-3660…
